quote: “Men, though they must die, are not born in order to die but in order to begin.”
source: Hannah Arendt, The Human Condition, ch. V, §34, p. 246 (University of Chicago Press, 1958)

evidence.where: Polytropy’s section by section reading of The Human Condition (paragraph 34.6, p. 246) and Adriana Cavarero, A Child Has Been Born unto Us: Arendt on Birth, citing Arendt 1998, 246; the 1998 second edition keeps the 1958 pagination
evidence.edition: The Human Condition, University of Chicago Press, 1958; second edition 1998, same pagination
evidence.locator: ch. V (Action), §34 (Unpredictability and the Power of Promise), p. 246

reason: The words appear verbatim on p. 246 as the close of a longer sentence (“like an ever-present reminder that men, though they must die, are not born in order to die but in order to begin”); the excerpt only capitalises the first word. Work, section and page as proposed.
